Verdicts need proof: Shorts compared with the same UK day's Shorts, shrink 12, push or cut back only with a 90% interval clear of typical and both halves of the data agreeing, and a 14-day pause and retest instead of a permanent stop

Exploration and diversity guardrails: 1 Short in 5 a day explores (a category drawn evenly from the day's packs, every test arm, look and posting quarter drawn evenly), every category at least 5% of the mix (1 a day, 2 at 40 a day) and none over 35%, no look option over 70% while any option has under 30 measured Shorts
No writer model over 35% of the day's boards until it has 10 measured Shorts, and writer scores shrunk on the log scale (5 Shorts' worth)

Measurement fixes: the topic source reaches shorts.csv, retention capped at 100%, looks and voices scored on engaged views (not swiping away) instead of still watching at 3 seconds, only verdict changes the writer acts on are logged; Instagram skip rate, reposts and Facebook views of crossposted Reels recorded

Originality and held-back titles: every Short makes a point of its own from the pack's facts, never the article's order or wording; titles under 50 characters, the searched name first, the answer held back, no question titles; statement hooks, one_detail and a moving camera as the prompt's defaults; Claude's editor follows the same title rules

Title emoji test: half the Shorts carry no emoji in the title (test.title_emoji, 50/50 by Short number, independent of the replies test, locked to a winner once drivers.csv says push; the validator and shape() hold each arm)

Charlie's Claude allowance first: Claude edits at most 4 boards a day, chosen at random from 3 in 10 passing boards so the editor test stays measured across the day; no Claude-written test boards; at most 3 Claude calls a write run (was 12 edits, 4 boards and 6 calls a run: 15 calls on 24 October)

Model lists: Groq's static list follows its limits page (gpt-oss-120b, qwen3.8-27b, gpt-oss-20b; Llama 3.3 70B and Kimi K2 are gone), its Orpheus voices are never tried as writers; SambaNova Cloud added as a free provider (DeepSeek V3.1, gpt-oss-120b, Llama 3.3 70B, 20 a day each), dormant until SAMBANOVA_API_KEY exists
Facebook on a probe: 1 Reel a day with a short caption (the title and 3 hashtags, no link) until a week shows plays; then the ramp resumes by itself
Clip takes argue rather than narrate: the spoken intro and outro add an argument, comparison or verdict the footage doesn't, never a description of the picture (recorded as test_take_style)
Hub Overview: Your actions this week (status/actions.json and needs-charlie issues) at the top; views by day a month at a time, live counter until YouTube's figure arrives

Watchlist of 22 dated events (15 on) from the calendar research, with one cap across the watchlist (a third of the day's Shorts; launch, then surging, then build-up) and per-item after_days and places
Hub shows the learning loop's pause and retest verdicts, and the title emoji test is scored from each board's assigned arm

Render path: a Short YouTube can't take yet (its daily limit, or the keys missing) is held as its draft preview in boards/ready, approved, and publish.py uploads it hourly without a new render; a board file holding a JSON list or string is rejected instead of stopping the whole plan; no upload call after a quota refusal

Saves merge by key: status files, clips/submit.csv and analytics/hourly.csv merge key by key or row by row when two workflows push at once (pipeline/merge_driver.py, .gitattributes), so no run drops another's Instagram, engage or submitted keys

Fewer idle runs: alerts start a runner only for failures (plus the evening and a 2-hourly recovery check), the render plan job and the early clips social run stop before installing anything, publish ignores the reserve before 18:20 UK, one trends run at a time, the whisper model is cached, old draft previews and clip files are pruned weekly, and a Pages workflow waits for Charlie's one-click switc

Mac Chrome run made small: a 3.5 KB card (docs/CHROME_JOBS.md, was 18.5 KB) plus python3 pipeline/mac_rows.py, which lists the Vyro rows to submit (newest first, places left per account), Content Rewards rescues, occasional and open one-off jobs, says NOTHING TO DO when there is nothing, and marks rows (done) so the Mac never opens clips/submit.csv; jobs waiting on Charlie stop being re-asked

Channel Instagram keys refreshed weekly by the identity audit (IG_<CHANNEL>_TOKEN into tokens/instagram_<channel>.enc, used in place of the secret by the clips runs and the audit); channel Facebook Page keys and Instagram keys near their end without a refresh raise one needs-charlie issue; the IG_TOKEN seed running out is no longer a renew alert

Model chain time savers: a writing model that times out once is passed over for the run (wait 180 s, was 240 s and 2 timeouts); a keyed provider that refuses 3 calls (a refused key at once) is passed over for the run; Groq answers within 3,500 tokens with one smaller retry on too large

Token and API efficiency: CLAUDE.md corrected and leaner with a token-budget rule; Haiku subagents in .claude/agents (quickplay-logs, quickplay-data, quickplay-tests, quickplay-docs) for log reading, numbers, tests and dated lines; the hub keeps GitHub API answers 10 minutes, asks nothing while hidden and waits for GitHub's reset after a 403

Volume test judged after 14 days on each UK day's numbers (daily YouTube views and the day's Shorts' 24-hour views, 90% intervals over days), not the 7-day snapshot ratio; 15 a day stays unless both are clearly lower

Act at 3 hours: a Short in the top fifth at 3 hours (2x the median at 3 hours, 20+ views) is a breakout at once, so its follow-up is written while the topic is hot; no third follow-up on a subject, none in a paused category, never a dead Short

Factorial test round 1: every Short takes an arm of hook (statement or number), length (25 to 34 s or 35 to 44 s), title wording (search phrase or curiosity) and first frame (cover or photo), each 50/50 and independent; settles at 70 measured Shorts an arm

Diversity floors: every category at least 7% of the day (was 5%), Gaming held at 15% until 26 November for the GTA 6 window, and no writer model over 35% of the day until it has 20 measured Shorts (was 10)

Instagram picks its own Reels: by category fit on Instagram (Gaming and Sport first until 15 Reels are measured, then Instagram's own numbers), 1 in 4 an exploration pick, at most 2 a run, capped at 8 a day (4 after Meta pushes back)

Instagram tests, each half the Reels and recorded on the post: trial reels (shown first to non-followers, graduated by Meta, SS_PERFORMANCE), a short caption (the spoken hook and 3 hashtags), posting in the UK morning (06:00 to 10:00) against as soon as public; the cover frame inside the opening beat

Writer-model test: groq gpt-oss-120b against Gemini Flash for the writing step, 6 boards in 10 drawn 50/50 by board number while both have a model (factpack.writer_test), the arm's model asked first unless the 35% cap says no; writer_arm (assigned) and writer_arm_used recorded, judged as assigned

Content review edits: the hook names the best-known person, band or team in its first four words (number arm too) and then the result; true stories and evergreen open on the result, never a question, Did you know or a date (validator warnings V1 to V4 give a board one fixing round); each length arm held to its word range; a 50/50 title test, news stated against answer held back, beside the title e

Clips social cap counts the last 24 hours, Content Rewards refusals named by the failed check (already, window, linked), Facebook's missing sign-in logged, the clips log kept across runs

Each beat's picture is chosen by relevance (SigLIP 2 scores the first 8 candidates against the beat's words, near-duplicates dropped) instead of the search's first hit; YuNet replaces the Haar cascade for face framing and the clips' person finder

changes.change: hub kept with the repository private: pages.yml copies docs/*.html and the static files they use (an explicit allowlist, no data leaves the private repo: never Markdown, JSON, CSV, status, analytics, tokens or boards) to the public org-site repo, and the hub reads the private repo in the browser with a read-only token that stays in Charlie's browser

the hub inside GitHub: README.md is the repo front page, a Markdown hub GitHub renders natively (actions, YPP table, a mermaid line of engaged views, contests and ledger verdicts, keys with fix links, channels), written by pipeline/hub_md.py from the files docs/hub.html reads and rebuilt in the hourly analytics commit and after the key audit; the old README is docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md; docs/hub.html a

sameness guard (pipeline/sameness.py): each draft is scored against the same channel's last 14 days of Shorts (narration 3-grams, title pattern, opening, look, format and series); over config sameness.max_pair 0.30 the writer asks the same model once to rewrite with the overlap named, then drops it; a recipe holding 35% of a channel's window is swapped for another in the planner (mega and the rese

frozen control group (pipeline/control.py, analytics/control_recipe.json frozen 2026-10-28): 10% of normal quota Shorts on the main channel (a seeded draw per board, never mega, reserve, follow-up, breaking, series part or exploration) are written with the recipe as it stood on the freeze day and the first free slot; marked control_arm 1 and left out of drivers, round, channel drivers, subscriber

False-winner control and re-test before lock-in: every verdict pass (drivers, round, channel drivers, evolve) now computes a p-value from the same t test its interval uses and applies Benjamini-Hochberg at analysis.fdr_q 0.10; a would-be winner that fails shows as running (luck check). An adopted winner enters confirming: 20% of eligible Shorts keep the previous choice until 20 a side are measured

Better targets: views_7d and views_28d per Short in shorts.csv from the existing hourly curves (no new YouTube calls), yt_feed_pct in the drivers outcome table, a channel-day subscriber table analytics/subs_daily.csv with an advisory ridge model analytics/subs_model.md, and ledger metrics feed_share, views_7d_median and subs_day. Helps both YPP numbers: subscribers (500 or 1,000) and Shorts views.

Joint model (pipeline/joint.py, numpy 2.5.3 pinned in analytics.yml): one regularised regression of log 24-hour views over the same-UK-day channel median on every test factor, channel, heat, weekday and category by factor interactions, seeded bootstrap intervals, opening factors also on engaged share; writes analytics/joint.csv and joint.md.
